scope: Six cervical indications across five monotherapy or concurrent chemoradiation protocols.

course: Pages 1–2. On each radiation treatment day scheduled for chemotherapy, infuse cisplatin 40 mg/m² over 60 minutes before radiation. Plan five weekly infusions. Further weekly cisplatin with ongoing radiation is a consultant decision. Defer chemotherapy when radiation is cancelled until radiation resumes.
eligibility_and_exclusions: Page 1. Definitive treatment (a) covers FIGO IIB–IVA cervical SCC, adenosquamous carcinoma and adenocarcinoma. Some IB3 and IIA cases require MDT discussion. Postoperative treatment (e) is for the same histologies with unexpected pathological nodal involvement.
Page 2. ECOG 0–2 and adequate organ/marrow function. Exclusions include pre-existing renal impairment, significant hearing impairment or tinnitus, hypersensitivity, pregnancy and breastfeeding.
assessment: Pages 2–3. Assess hydration, electrolytes and renal function. Table 1 delays chemotherapy for ANC <1 or platelets <100 (both ×10⁹/L).

Page 4, Tables 2–3. At CrCl 40–49 use 50% of the original dose and at 50–59 use 75%. Below 40 mL/min cisplatin is not recommended. A 50% dose may be considered on haemodialysis. The printed integer bands do not resolve decimal intervals 49–50 or 59–60. Grade 2 peripheral neuropathy warrants 25% reduction; grades 3–4 warrant omission.

course: Page 1. Carboplatin AUC 2 IV over 30 minutes every seven days alongside radiotherapy. Six cycles unless progression, unacceptable toxicity or truncated radiation. The subsequent adjuvant regimen described for head and neck cancer does not apply to the cervical indication.
eligibility_and_exclusions: Pages 1, 3. Locally advanced cervical cancer when cisplatin is contraindicated or not tolerated, ECOG 0–2. Pregnancy, breastfeeding and hypersensitivity are exclusions. Specialist desensitisation after a prior mild carboplatin reaction is exceptional.
assessment: Pages 2, 4. Calvert dosing requires absolute GFR in mL/min capped at 125. Use measured GFR where feasible. An estimated result requires a fresh creatinine within 48 hours. For isotope GFR, consider reassessment when current creatinine exceeds 110% of its value at measurement.

Page 3, Table 1. Assess treatment-day ANC and the platelet count at any stage during the cycle. ANC 0.5–0.99 or platelets 50–99 require delay until recovery. ANC <0.5, platelets <50 or febrile neutropenia require delay and consideration of 25% reduction in subsequent cycles.
Page 4, Table 2. Clearance below 60 mL/min increases myelosuppression risk. Above 20 through 30 mL/min requires extreme caution. At 20 mL/min or below, avoid administration.

course: Page 1. Cemiplimab 350 mg IV over 30 minutes every 21 days, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
eligibility_and_exclusions: Pages 1–2. Adults with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer progressing on or after platinum chemotherapy; ECOG 0–2 and adequate organ/marrow function. PD-L1 testing is not an eligibility criterion. Exclude active CNS metastases, significant active infection requiring therapy, systemic immunosuppression (prednisolone equivalent >10 mg/day or another immunosuppressive medicine), hypersensitivity, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inhaled and topical steroids are excluded from the systemic steroid threshold. Check prior PD-1/PD-L1 treatment against the Irish guidance.
assessment: Page 2. FBC, renal and liver profile, glucose and thyroid function at baseline; hepatitis B/C screening. Check FBC, renal and liver profile and glucose before each cycle; TSH every 3–6 weeks.
Pages 3–5, Table 2. Withhold for grade 2 pneumonitis; discontinue permanently for recurrent grade 2 or grade 3–4. Withhold at grade 2 immune nephritis and permanently discontinue at grade 3–4.

Page 3, Table 2; Libtayo SmPC 4.2/4.4. Investigate other causes of abnormal liver tests. Once attributed to immune hepatitis, withhold for AST/ALT >3 to ≤5 ×ULN or bilirubin >1.5 to ≤3 ×ULN. Permanently discontinue above the upper thresholds. The assessment withholds for urgent clinical review while attribution is pending across all 00812 indications.

course: Pages 1–2. After completing combination induction, pembrolizumab 200 mg IV over 30 minutes every 21 days. Continue to progression or unacceptable toxicity. At 24 months with a sustained response and no progression, consider stopping. Continuing beyond 24 months is individualised.

The monotherapy protocols give two approved maintenance schedules. They do not prescribe a universal cycle or time point to switch from the three-week to the six-week interval. Verify induction completion, the selected interval and the last administration before scheduling.
eligibility_and_exclusions: Pages 1 and 4. Adults with persistent, recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer, ECOG 0–2, validated tumour PD-L1 CPS ≥1. Establish that induction has finished. A TPS result does not establish the required CPS.

Page 4. Hypersensitivity is an exclusion. Serious autoimmune disease history, baseline systemic immunosuppression, active infection requiring therapy, untreated brain metastases, and interstitial lung disease history are cautions. Consult Irish prior checkpoint-inhibitor guidance.
assessment: Pages 4–7. Monitor renal/liver/thyroid function and glucose. Withhold for grade 2 pneumonitis and permanently discontinue at grade 3–4 or recurrent grade 2. Clinically attributed immune nephritis or hepatitis uses its specific laboratory and recovery thresholds; evaluate other causes of abnormal results.

course: Pages 1–2. After completing combination induction, pembrolizumab 400 mg IV over 30 minutes every 42 days. Continue to progression or unacceptable toxicity. At 24 months with a sustained response and no progression, consider stopping. Continuing beyond 24 months is individualised.

The monotherapy protocols give two approved maintenance schedules. They do not prescribe a universal cycle or time point to switch from the three-week to the six-week interval. Verify induction completion, the selected interval and the last administration before scheduling.
eligibility_and_exclusions: Pages 1 and 3. Adults with persistent, recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer, ECOG 0–2, validated tumour PD-L1 CPS ≥1. Establish that induction has finished. A TPS result does not establish the required CPS.

Page 4. Hypersensitivity is an exclusion. Serious autoimmune disease history, baseline systemic immunosuppression, active infection requiring therapy, untreated brain metastases, and interstitial lung disease history are cautions. Consult Irish prior checkpoint-inhibitor guidance.
assessment: Pages 4–7. Monitor renal/liver/thyroid function and glucose. Withhold for grade 2 pneumonitis and permanently discontinue at grade 3–4 or recurrent grade 2. Clinically attributed immune nephritis or hepatitis uses its specific laboratory and recovery thresholds; evaluate other causes of abnormal results.

00817.title: NCCP 00817 v3
00817.clinical_use: Pages 1–2. Combination pembrolizumab/paclitaxel/carboplatin induction at 21-day intervals (six to eight cycles, with ongoing clinical benefit and clinician discretion beyond six), followed by maintenance pembrolizumab 200 mg every 21 days.

00811.title: NCCP 00811 v3
00811.clinical_use: Pages 1–2. Bevacizumab-containing induction uses the same six-to-eight-cycle framework. Its maintenance table continues pembrolizumab 200 mg and bevacizumab 15 mg/kg every 21 days. Confirm the intended bevacizumab plan before opening monotherapy.

prior-pd1.title: NCCP previous PD-1/PD-L1 treatment guidance, version 2 (27 April 2026)
prior-pd1.clinical_use: Page 1. For the same unresectable/metastatic condition, review prior checkpoint treatment. An alternative approved drug may be considered for intolerance; specific licensed reimbursed indications can supersede general guidance. Continuing pembrolizumab from induction to maintenance is continuation of the same course.

keytruda.title: EMA Keytruda IV product information
keytruda.clinical_use: Annex I, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4 and 5.1. Cross-check the cervical CPS indication, IV schedule, immune toxicity assessment and KEYNOTE-826 evidence. Irish NCCP documents establish the local maintenance routes.

libtayo.title: EMA Libtayo product information
libtayo.clinical_use: Annex I, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4 and 5.1. Cross-check post-platinum cervical monotherapy, IV schedule, assessment of alternative causes of immune toxicity and EMPOWER-Cervical 1 evidence.

findings: Added the missing cervical duration context for 00419b so a cervical pathway shows its six concurrent weekly doses.

Applied immune-mediated hepatitis attribution across all cemiplimab indications. An abnormal result with attribution pending generates an urgent hold. Confirmed immune hepatitis uses Table 2 boundaries. When the two tests give different severity bands, the more severe action governs.

Verified the common cemiplimab safety action for cervical cancer, cutaneous SCC, and absent or unrecognised indication input. The assessment accepts the published NCCP indication code when the protocol maps it to one unambiguous native selector; unrecognised values still return a validation error alongside any independently indicated hold.
